To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have developed a new methodology to estimate the classification accuracy of a BCI based on the auditory DL task, which can be applied to any other BCI that employs the same task.
the auditory Brain-Computer Interfaces can be modeled as a Binary Phase Shift Keying receiver and that this model allows us to predict the accuracy on a trial-to-trial basis.
we have developed an auditory Brain-Computer interface with accuracy prediction.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an auditory BCI with a priori estimation of accuracy.
the design of a DL-BCI that can be used in applications that require high accuracy.
the improvement of the performance of DL-BCI by estimating the accuracy of the system in advance and by using this information for the design of the system.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the Bayesian approach is a promising methodology to estimate the accuracy of the DL-BCIs, which could be applied in future research to improve their performance and to make them adequate for more applications that require a certain accuracy.
we developed a novel method to predict the accuracy of the DL-BCIs, and that this method can be employed in the design of auditory BCIs to achieve a specific performance.
this work presents a novel methodology for the design of auditory BCIs that allows the estimation of the classification accuracy on trial-by-trial bases.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have developed a novel DL-BCI that can be tuned for any application and any user, which is a significant improvement in comparison with the existing DL-BCI systems that are not able to adapt to the user or to the application.

the proposed approach can be used as an aid to design DL-BCIs for a specific application by defining the target accuracy and the corresponding signal-to-noise ratios that guarantee that accuracy, thus, avoiding the need of extensive experiments to define the target accuracy and its corresponding signal-to-noises ratios.

the Bayesian approach allowed us to predict in advance, on a trial-by trial basis, the accuracy of the DL-BCIs, which in turn allowed us to set the target accuracy and thus the signal-to-noiseratio for a given application.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we provide an accurate and efficient way of estimating the accuracy of DL-BCIs in advance.
this methodology can be used to design DL-BCIs for any application that requires a specific level of accuracy.
the DL-BCIs can now be designed with an accuracy guarantee, thus making them suitable for applications that require a very high accuracy, such as controlling a robotic arm.
